title: Shabbetai the Fruit-Hoarder
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yoma 82b relates that a pregnant woman smelled food. The case came before R' Chanina, who said to whisper to her that it was Yom Kippur. They whispered, but she was not calmed. He applied to the unborn child the verse “The wicked are estranged from the womb.” She gave birth to Shabbetai, the fruit-hoarder.
In Bava Batra 90b, Rabbi Yochanan [supplied אר״י] says, “For example, Shabbetai the hoarder of fruit.” The supplied text repeats the locator and reporting phrase.

notes.text: The Bava Batra citation repeats90b and the reporting phrase in the supplied text. The speaker initials R”Y remain unresolved. Shabbetai and Shabtai, and the Aramaic/Hebrew forms of fruit-hoarder, are supplied variants.

The saved whole Davidson BavaBatra90b scalar explicitly spells Rabbi Yochanan as the reporter and Shabtai the fruit-hoarder as his example. It supports this exact אר״י expansion, superseding the older unsupported Yehudah expansion and later unresolved-initials note. Supplied צ: אר״י duplication and Shabbetai/Shabtai, peiri/peirot remain visible without asserting a proven printed dittography. YomKippur whisper content and the unborn-child referent are inherited contextual readings of the Yoma narrative, not new whole-scalar verification this wake.

The printed notice repeats the word “her” at the line break and repeats the Bava Batra locator and reporting formula. Bava Batra 90b names Rabbi Yochanan as the speaker. The story begins at the end of Yoma 82b with R’ Chanina and concludes at the start of 83a with Shabbetai’s birth. The preceding, separate story explicitly gives the words whispered about Yom Kippur and ends with R’ Yochanan’s birth.
